questions.question: What color is a warning sign?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Makes you more visible to other drivers.
Should only be used at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Reflective material on your helmet makes you easier to see. Use it day and night for safety.

questions.question: If there are hazards on your left, where should you ride in your lane?
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a motorcycle, what should you do about your blind spot?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Slow down and let other vehicles pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show your blind spots. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: When will a helmet NOT protect you as well as it should?

options.text: If it has a DOT sticker.

questions.explanation: A helmet must have a DOT sticker, fit snugly, and have no cracks or damage to protect you properly. Do not use a cracked helmet.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Most conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles happen at intersections. Use extra caution when approaching and crossing intersections.

questions.question: When getting ready to pass a vehicle on the left, what lane position should you use?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane to see the passing lane better before passing.

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may drift into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You will stay in your lane.
It is okay because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to drift into another lane or off the road. Slow down before turning.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, how should you hold the handgrips?

options.text: Remove your helmet so it does not cover your face.

questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding over rough surfaces to maintain control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. They tell you the speed rules for that road.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, where should the passenger sit?

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle nor in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: The passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Limiting the distance ridden in one day

questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks and do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Do not take artificial stimulants. They can be very dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: You are about to slow down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is smaller than a car's. Flash your brake light to alert other drivers, especially when you need to slow down faster than they may expect.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Make sure the mirrors are clean.
Make sure the clutch works smoothly.

questions.explanation: After mounting, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes all work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is open.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars look:
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make objects appear farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: A properly-fitted motorcycle should:

options.text: Allow the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
Have a seat level with the rider's waist.
Have a seat 10 inches above the rider's waist.
Have a seat 10 inches below the rider's waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the rider to touch the ground with their feet while seated.
questions.explanation: A properly fitted motorcycle allows your feet to touch the ground while you are seated. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests when riding.

questions.question: When being passed, which of these is NOT a potential hazard?

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.explanation: When being passed, watch for the passing vehicle's mirrors. Be aware of wind gusts and objects that may be thrown by passengers. These are all hazards to motorcyclists.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: The best way to help others see you at an intersection is to keep your headlight on. Always ride with your headlight on when the motorcycle is running.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following except:

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Increase your ability to be seen by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, keeps you out of other drivers' blind spots, avoids hazards, protects your lane, shows your intentions, helps you avoid wind blasts, and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to look for cross traffic before proceeding.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign, then edge forward to look for cross traffic before proceeding.
questions.explanation: First, stop where the stop sign indicates. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean your body forward to look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to see if traffic is coming. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while you look.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets if possible. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that might catch on the motorcycle and should lean with the operator when turning. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only on slippery roads.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use if used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you start riding.

questions.question: If using a sidecar to transport a load, you should:

options.text: Allow the load to move freely.
Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not shift and affect handling. Place loads toward the back of the sidecar to prevent the nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: The body generally eliminates one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed to estimate remaining alcohol. In this case, 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals about 4 drinks remaining.
